summary: Offboard: Contractor — Rotate keys, deprovision accounts, and recover hardware for departing contract engineer
description: Connor Blake (contractor) from Eng-Infra is ending their engagement. People Ops requested a coordinated offboard: revoke access, rotate any service account keys they created, remove org memberships, and schedule equipment pickup. HR is asking for confirmation of timing and whether any access should be retained for knowledge transfer. Ticket combines account deprovision tasks and policy questions on contractor access retention.
accounts_to_remove: G Suite / Google Workspace: connor.blake@contractor.redwood.com — remove from org
GitHub: connor-blake — remove org membership and team access
AWS IAM: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:user/connor.blake — revoke console keys
GCP: project-level IAM bindings and any personal service account keys
equipment_items: MacBook Pro 14" — serial: C02ABC12345 — asset tag: RD-IT-875
USB-C Docking Station — asset tag: RD-IT-542
service_accounts: infra-deployer-sa — created 2025-11-02 — keys stored in Connor's GCP user — ACTION: rotate and move to central KMS-managed SA if still needed
pipeline-runner-sa — used by nightly jobs — ACTION: audit permissions and rotate keys
legacy-test-sa — low-usage, candidate for deletion if no owners found
policy_questions: 1) Do contractor accounts get immediately disabled at EOD on last day or 48 hours after to allow handover?
2) For service accounts created by contractors, do we automatically rotate keys and reassign ownership to a full-time engineer, or delete if unused for 30 days?
3) Are contractors eligible for device return pickup by IT or should they send devices via prepaid shipping?
4) Retention policy for contractor GitHub commits: should repo access be archived or retained under a read-only org team?
steps_to_complete: (1) Disable Okta user + force MFA token invalidation
(2) Deactivate Slack and remove from all private channels; export pinned messages if requested by manager
(3) Remove GitHub org membership and rotate any deploy keys where username 'connor-blake' was used
(4) Audit GCP/AWS for active keys linked to Connor; rotate or revoke immediately
(5) Inventory listed hardware, open IT pickup task, mark assets 'pending return' in Asset DB
(6) Audit service accounts listed and either reassign ownership or schedule deletion after 30-day TTL
(7) Confirm with People Ops whether a 48-hour grace period is permitted for handover docs; if yes, schedule partial disable then final remove
(8) Document actions and close ticket with resolution notes and asset receipts
